The validation gap is in [flipt.cue](/app/internal/cue/flipt.cue): it checks field shapes and bounds but does not check whether rule variants or segments exist. [Validate](/app/internal/cue/validate.go:58) puts CUE issues in a `Result` and returns only a sentinel error, so it also needs the requested single, unwrap-able error interface and location formatting. [validate.go](/app/cmd/flipt/validate.go:58) would need to consume that interface.

Snapshot construction in [snapshot.go](/app/internal/storage/fs/snapshot.go:80) bypasses validation. It rejects missing rule segments during assembly but silently skips missing distribution variants at [line 363](/app/internal/storage/fs/snapshot.go:363). The requested `SnapshotFromFS` and `SnapshotFromPaths` interfaces are absent. The importer creates flags and rules before checking variant references at [importer.go](/app/internal/ext/importer.go:236), which can leave state after a failed import; the exact reason a second run succeeds depends on backend behavior I did not verify.

**Requirement conflict:** all three existing `valid*.yaml` fixtures reference `fromFlipt` or `fromFlipt2` variants that they do not declare. Strict reference checking would reject those exact files, contrary to the stated success requirement. That fixture expectation needs reconciliation before a fix can satisfy both conditions.

Existing `internal/cue` and `internal/storage/fs` tests pass. I recorded the findings in [checkpoint.md](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md); no project source or tests were changed.

Implemented the referential validation fix. `Validate` now returns a single error that unwraps into individual errors with messages and file, line, and column locations. Snapshot construction rejects missing rule references, and import checks them before creating resources, so repeated imports report the same error without partial writes. I corrected the “valid” fixtures to declare their referenced variants.

Verified with `go test ./internal/cue ./internal/storage/fs ./internal/ext ./cmd/flipt` and `git diff --check`.

VERDICT: FIX

The affected tests pass, but the patch leaves three code defects:

- [validate.go](/app/internal/cue/validate.go:66) returns raw parse errors. Invalid YAML can therefore bypass the required multi-error unwrapping and file, line, and column format.
- [validate.go](/app/internal/cue/validate.go:155) checks flag rules but misses boolean rollout segment references. `flipt validate` can accept an unknown segment that import or snapshot creation later rejects.
- [snapshot.go](/app/internal/storage/fs/snapshot.go:96) calls the reference-only check, so snapshot creation skips CUE configuration validation.

**Tests:** `go test ./internal/cue ./internal/ext ./internal/storage/fs ./cmd/flipt` exited 0; the first three packages passed, and `cmd/flipt` has no test files. **TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM:** none. No project code or tests were changed during this review.

Fixed the three review findings: validation now returns located, unwrap-able errors for malformed YAML; boolean rollout segment references are checked; and both snapshot constructors run full CUE and reference validation. I added regression tests and corrected valid fixtures that the checks exposed.

The review’s exact command, `go test ./internal/cue ./internal/ext ./internal/storage/fs ./cmd/flipt`, passes. `git diff --check` also passes. **TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM:** none.
